region: Northern temperate and boreal forests of Europe, Asia and North America
description: Spruce is a pale, light, straight-grained softwood sold as construction lumber, pallet stock and the 'S' in SPF framing. Norway spruce and Sitka spruce are also prized for guitar and violin soundboards.

hazards.summary: A small number of workers have developed allergic asthma from spruce dust, confirmed by specific IgE antibodies to spruce and, in one carpenter, by challenge testing. The evidence comes from Norway spruce (Picea abies) and spruce used in Polish and German workshops.
The UK HSE lists spruce as a cause of respiratory problems. A Canadian study of sawmill workers handling pine and spruce found lower lung function and more wheeze than in a comparison group.

Finnish workers exposed to pine or spruce dust developed allergic skin rashes, often on the face, and reacted on patch testing to the sawdust and to rosin (colophony). The reports do not always separate spruce from pine.
The UK HSE notes that spruce may make skin more sensitive to sunlight. No primary report was found to confirm this.
All wood dust is classified as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses. This applies to this wood like every other species.

known_compounds.name: peroxidase enzymes
known_compounds.role: Proteins identified as IgE-binding allergens in spruce wood in one carpenter

known_compounds.name: colophony (rosin) and abietic acid
known_compounds.role: Resin components that patients with pine/spruce dust dermatitis reacted to on patch testing

related_species_note: In the documented case, the same patient also had IgE to pine and larch wood, so sensitization may extend across softwoods.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed Sitka spruce (Picea sitchensis) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Creamy white to very pale straw-colored wood with a faint pinkish-brown cast and little contrast between heartwood and sapwood. Fine, even texture with straight, tightly spaced growth rings showing a gradual transition from pale earlywood to slightly darker latewood, a soft silky luster, and no visible pores. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of spruce with pale creamy-white wood and fine, straight, closely spaced growth rings.
notes_internal: Genus entry. Image prompt uses Sitka spruce as the representative species. Schlunssen-2018 also cites Oertmann 1993 and Kersten 1994 (German, Allergologie) for spruce asthma; not in PubMed, not verified, not cited. Estlander-2001 and Majamaa-2004 group pine and spruce; level 1 for skin is based on patch tests with sawdust, but species attribution is shared with pine. HSE photosensitization note has no primary source. ACGIH A4 (not classifiable) not added as a carcinogen_class row; leave to agency agent.
